name: Wei Cheng
bio: Wei Cheng (Wei Zheng, 魏徵, 580–643) was a statesman of the early Tang dynasty. He served first under the rebel Li Mi and then under Li Jiancheng, the crown prince, before Emperor Taizong took him into his own service. As chancellor he became known for plain speaking at court.

He is remembered chiefly as a counsellor, but a few poems survive in the Quan Tang shi. The best known, 述懷 (Shu huai, 'Setting Out My Feelings'), is thought to date from his journey to join the new dynasty, and ends on a famous line about loyalty between a man and his patron.

poems.title: 述懷 (Shu huai)
poems.author: Wei Cheng
poems.text:
中原初逐鹿，投筆事戎軒。
縱橫計不就，慷慨志猶存。
杖策謁天子，驅馬出關門。
請纓繫南粵，憑軾下東藩。
鬱紆陟高岫，出沒望平原。
古木鳴寒鳥，空山啼夜猿。
既傷千里目，還驚九折魂。
豈不憚艱險，深懷國士恩。
季布無二諾，侯嬴重一言。
人生感意氣，功名誰復論。
